audit.whatIsWrong: diff said FAV but diffRating said 8/10 — a favoured lane rated as one of the hardest in the pool, on a 54.96% win rate over 1785 games.
audit.why: The label and the number said opposite things.
audit.corrected: diffRating lowered to 4/10 to match FAV and the win rate; carryRating left at 8.5/10 because a scaled Swain genuinely takes over.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[2] said Skill, win[4] said Skill, win[5] and win[6] said Darius — while whys[2] says level 3 favours Darius, whys[4] says level 6 tilts to Swain, whys[5] calls first item a coin-flip and whys[6] gives Swain two-plus items. The packet chart reads Darius, Darius, Darius, Darius, Swain, Skill, Swain.
audit.why: Four rows contradicted their own explanations and the packet, and the late-game rows were inverted — the entry told the reader he wins the stage its own prose says he loses.
audit.corrected: Level 3 to Darius, Level 6 to Swain, First item to Skill, 2+ items to Swain.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interactions absent. Demonic Ascension lasts indefinitely only while Swain is draining a champion inside 650 units, so breaking away ends it. Vision of Empire (W) hands him a Soul Fragment whenever it catches a champion, so eating it directly feeds his healing. Nevermove (E) roots on the wave's RETURN and he can then pull the rooted target in.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions'; 'Champions hit are revealed and also grant Swain a Soul Fragment'; 'It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer.' Walking out of ult range is the counterplay to the ability the entry calls matchup-defining, and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: All three written in, with Demonic Ascension 120s, Nevermove 12s and Vision of Empire 22s at rank 1.

audit.why: The entry already tells you to build an early anti-heal component, which is right: Ravenous Flock heals off every Soul Fragment and permanently raises his max health, so Grievous Wounds beats stacking resistances here.

edits.before: Swain's R Demonic Ascension flips the fight: his sustain and AoE drain heal through your bleed, so don't extend a trade into his ult unless you have R ready to execute.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension (120s) flips the fight, but it only stays up while he drains a champion — walk out of the 650 range and the form ends, so break off rather than trade into the heal.

edits.before: Levels 1-4 Swain is a low-mobility mage you can walk down — sidestep his Q feathers and E root, then punish with Q Decimate poke.
edits.after: Levels 1-4 Swain is a low-mobility mage you walk down — sidestep Death's Hand, dodge Nevermove on its return, and punish with Q poke.

edits.before: At 6 his R drain swings the lane; a full-combo all-in trades into his healing, so only commit with R up to execute before Demonic Ascension out-heals you.
edits.after: At 6 the drain swings the lane, but it holds only while he drains a champion inside 650 — commit with R up to execute, or leave his range and let it expire.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Don’t fight into it. Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane.
edits.after: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — 120s, and it holds only while he is draining a champion inside 650 units, so walking out ends it. - Nevermove: 12s at rank 1 and it roots on the wave's return, then he pulls you in. - Vision of Empire: 22s, and every champion it catches feeds him a Soul Fragment and the heal that comes with it. - Apprehend: 26s at rank 1 — hold it for his step-up.

edits.before: His drain. Don’t fight into it. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: His drain, 120s. It ends when nobody is in range — leave rather than fight it.

edits.before: Whiffing Apprehend and then fighting anyway — without the pull you have no engage, and chasing through a wave bleeds you dry.
edits.after: Vision of Empire hands him a Soul Fragment off you, and that fragment is healing plus permanent health — sidestep the eye.

notes: The two late rows of the chart were inverted against the entry's own whys: it gave Darius First item and 2+ items while the prose said Swain out-sustains him at both. Demonic Ascension's uptime condition — it holds only while he is draining a champion in 650 range — is the counterplay to the ability the entry calls matchup-defining, and it was absent from all 17 fields. Packet suspectName 'Demonic Ascension's' is a FALSE POSITIVE: that is the real name of his R, with a possessive. diff FAV and diffRating 8/10 disagreed with each other; I moved the number, not the label.
